EMPIRICAL RESEARCH PLAN  
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

1. IDENTIFICATION STRATEGY
------------------------------------------------
Strategy:  Staggered-adoption Difference-in-Differences (DID) combined with an event-study specification for dynamics and with Triple-Differences (DDD) when we interact treatment with unionization.

Why appropriate:  
• The “treatment” (judicial recognition of an employment-at-will exception) occurs at clearly-dated, state-specific moments that differ across states between 1973-1995.  
• We observe an untreated counterfactual: states that have not yet (or never) adopted the exception in a given year.  
• Outcomes (temporary-help employment levels/shares, outsourcing shares) are available annually by state.  
• The staggered adoption lends itself to modern DID estimators that remain valid under treatment timing heterogeneity (e.g. Callaway-Sant’Anna 2021; Sun-Abraham 2021).  

We will therefore estimate:  
log(Y_st) = α + β Treat_st + γ_s + δ_t + X_st′θ + ε_st  
and the corresponding event-study:

log(Y_st) = α + Σ_{k≠-1} π_k Event_kst + γ_s + δ_t + X_st′θ + ε_st.

For union interaction we estimate:

log(Y_st) = α + β₁ Treat_st + β₂ Union_st + β₃ Treat_st×Union_st + γ_s + δ_t + X_st′θ + ε_st.

2. TREATMENT AND CONTROL
------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable:  
Treat_st = 1 if state s in year t has in force an “implied-contract” exception to employment at will (the exception most plausibly raising wrongful-discharge risk) and 0 otherwise. We will check robustness to alternative definitions: any exception; public-policy only; good-faith only.

Control group:  
States that, in year t, have not yet adopted the exception. These units form a valid contemporaneous counterfactual under the parallel-trends assumption.

Treatment timing / event date:  
Event date = first calendar year the state supreme court (or legislature) recognized the exception (coded from Morriss, Postic, BNA). Event time k = t-T_s where T_s is adoption year.

No RDD is envisaged; no running variable.

3. KEY IDENTIFYING ASSUMPTIONS
------------------------------------------------
A1. Parallel trends: In the absence of adoption, treated and yet-to-be-treated states would have experienced similar growth paths in temporary-help employment.  
Plausibility: States did not change doctrine in response to pre-existing trends in temporary-help specifically; decisions arose largely from idiosyncratic lawsuits. We will empirically test using pre-treatment event-study coefficients.

A2. No anticipation: Firms do not change outsourcing behavior until the decision becomes law. Judicial rulings are hard to forecast, so anticipation is limited.

A3. Stable unit treatment value (no spillovers): Outsourcing in an adopting state does not mechanically alter outcomes in non-adopting states. Most temporary-help firms operate locally, so geographic spillovers should be small.

A4. Treatment exogeneity conditional on controls: Timing of rulings is unrelated to other contemporaneous state policy shifts after controlling for state & year FE and observed covariates (union laws, demographics).

4. THREATS TO IDENTIFICATION & MITIGATION
------------------------------------------------
T1. Omitted simultaneous policy changes (e.g., workers’-comp reform, UI changes).  
Mitigation: Include controls for major labor regulations (minimum wage, UI replacement rate, right-to-work status) and state-specific linear or quadratic trends. Conduct placebo tests with those policies as “pseudo-treatments.”

T2. Heterogeneous treatment timing bias in two-way FE.  
Mitigation: Use modern DID estimators (Sun-Abraham sunab(), Callaway-Sant’Anna did::att_gt()) that are robust to such bias, report group-time ATTs.

T3. Measurement error in adoption dates.  
Mitigation: Cross-validate coding against multiple sources; perform ±1-year fuzzy adoption robustness; drop states with ambiguous dating.

5. R CODE OUTLINE
------------------------------------------------
```r
# Required packages
library(data.table)
library(fixest)          # modern DID & Sun-Abraham
library(did)             # Callaway-Sant’Anna
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Load data ------------------------------------------------------------
cbp   <- fread("state_cbp_1979_2000.csv")      # industry employment counts
cps   <- fread("state_cps_controls_1979_1995.csv")
union <- fread("state_union_1979_1995.csv")
law   <- fread("state_atwill_exceptions.csv")  # 0/1 by type
policy<- fread("state_other_policies.csv")

# 2. Merge & construct variables -----------------------------------------
dt <- Reduce(function(x,y) merge(x,y, by = c("state","year"), all = TRUE),
             list(cbp, cps, union, law, policy))

# Outcome: log share of temp help in nonfarm employment
dt[, temp_share := temp_help_emp / nonfarm_emp]
dt[, ltemp_share := log(temp_share + 1e-6)]   # avoid log(0)

# Treatment flags
dt[, treat_contract := implied_contract == 1]          # main
# Event-time dummies for Sun-Abraham (up to ±6 years)
dt <- sunab(dt, gvar = "adopt_year_contract", tvar = "year", ref.year = -1,
            add.att = FALSE)

# Control vars
controls <- c("avg_edu", "female_share", "age2529_share", "rtw_law",
              "state_minwage", "ui_replacement", "union_rate")

# 3. Main TWFE with Sun-Abraham event study ------------------------------
feols_main <- feols(ltemp_share ~ sunab(adopt_year_contract, year) + 
                    union_rate + .SD,
                    data = dt, .SDcols = controls,
                    fixef = ~ state + year, cluster = ~ state)

etable(feols_main, se = "cluster")

# 4. Callaway-Sant’Anna group-time ATT -----------------------------------
att <- att_gt(yname   = "ltemp_share",
              gname   = "adopt_year_contract",
              idname  = "state",
              tname   = "year",
              xformla = ~ union_rate + .,
              data    = dt)

ggdid(att)   # plot dynamic ATTs

# 5. Robustness: placebo using Business Services NEC ---------------------
dt[, lbiz_share := log(biz_services_nec_emp / nonfarm_emp + 1e-6)]
placebo <- feols(lbiz_share ~ sunab(adopt_year_contract, year) + .SD,
                 data = dt, .SDcols = controls,
                 fixef = ~ state + year, cluster = ~ state)

etable(feols_main, placebo, se = "cluster")
```

6. EXPECTED RESULTS
------------------------------------------------
Economic reasoning: By shielding employers from wrongful-discharge liability when they hire temps instead of direct employees, the implied-contract exception should raise the relative demand for temporary-help workers. I expect:

β > 0 : 3–6 percent increase in temp-help employment share within 5 years after adoption (≈0.03–0.06 log points).  
Interaction: Effect larger where unionization is high, because unions raise firing costs for direct employees; thus β₃ > 0.

7. VALIDITY CHECKLIST SELF-ASSESSMENT (DID)
------------------------------------------------
C1: No systematic pre-trends (parallel trends)………………… 0.8  
C2: No anticipation………………………………………………………… 0.9  
C3: No spillovers / SUTVA……………………………………………… 0.8  
C4: Correct treatment timing / stable coding…………………… 0.7  
C5: Robustness across estimators & outcomes…………………… 0.8

Overall, while plausible, careful pre-trend testing and robustness work are essential.
